_comment: klt erc supply spec for layout/modexp.gds -- the T1 item 11
(power delivery, structural) read for this repo (issue #129).
Regenerate the committed report with:
klt erc layout/modexp.gds layout/erc/erc-supply-spec.json \
--format json > layout/erc/modexp-erc-supply-report.json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- stackup[0] MUST carry role: "gate" (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at poly rather than at li1. active_layer (65/20,
diff.drawing) makes the antenna denominator poly n diff instead of
raw poly area, which keeps tap/filler/decap-cell poly -- real poly
with no gate oxide -- out of gates[] entirely instead of reporting
non-physical antenna ratios for them (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area'). sky130's PDK lyp
(libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp, open_pdks c6d73a35) names
poly.drawing 66/20 and diff.drawing 65/20; klayout-tools' curated
sky130 deck (decks/sky130.py) quotes the same two numbers.
- li1/met1..met5 are the levels this block actually uses: the GDS
and all five metals), and flow/par-modexp.json's power.straps sit
on met1 (followpins), met4 and met5 -- so every PDN strap layer is
inside this stackup, which item 11's Digital column requires.
- label_layer 67/5 (li1.label) and 68/5 (met1.label) are the only
two layers this merged GDS puts standard-cell PG pin text on:
VPWR x 21 / VGND x 21 on 67/5 and VPWR x 3074 / VGND x 3074 on
68/5 (verified by scanning the GDS text labels directly). met5's
72/5 carries only the two top-level PDN pin texts VDD and VSS --
deliberately given NO label_layer here because those names are not
declared in nets[] (see below), so declaring the text layer would
add nothing to any check.
- GDS layer numbers are sky130's own, resolved from the pinned PDK's
libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp (open_pdks c6d73a35, the
docs/environment.md pin) and cross-checked against klayout-tools'
curated sky130 deck layer table -- not copied from another PDK's
spec: licon1.drawing 66/44, mcon.drawing 67/44,
via.drawing 68/44, via2.drawing 69/44, via3.drawing 70/44,
via4.drawing 71/44 bridge the stack in the 'via named after its
lower layer' convention the deck itself documents.
- nets[]: VPWR and VGND both kind: "supply", which is what makes a
short between them report as the severe erc.supply_short rather
than the general erc.multiply_driven_net. Each must resolve to
exactly ONE electrical island: erc.unconnected_net fires on zero
matches (nothing carries that label at all) AND on more than one
(the rail is split into pieces that never touch) -- so ZERO
findings of that rule over the 3095 VPWR and 3095 VGND labels is
exactly the 'one island per supply' verdict, not merely an
absence. The split-rail case is precisely the no-PDN failure mode
this spec exists to detect.
- Why VPWR/VGND and not the top-level VDD/VSS: the DEF's
SPECIALNETS section joined the rails as 'VDD (* VPB) (* VPWR)'
and 'VSS (* VNB) (* VGND)' -- one island per polarity carrying
two label spellings. klt erc treats two different declared names
on one island as a short, so declaring both spellings would
misreport the intended join as erc.supply_short. The cell-side
spelling (VPWR/VGND, 3095 labels each across li1.label +
met1.label) is declared because it is the far stronger test:
every standard-cell row rail and every tap cell must stitch into
the same single island as the PDN. The lone 72/5 VDD/VSS pin
texts sit on those same islands by the DEF's own join.
- There is deliberately NO ties[] section here, and that is a
recorded gap rather than an oversight: declaring one on a real
routed standard-cell layout collapses the whole design into one
electrical island and reports a FALSE erc.supply_short -- filed
upstream as klayout-tools#2169 (reproduced four ways in
gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034). Because ties[] is omitted,
erc.missing_tie is NOT COMPUTED by this run (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely -> erc.missing_tie is never
computed') -- its zero count in the committed report is an
absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. README.md in this
directory names what IS admissible evidence that the well ties
are real and connected, and what is missing.
